unit_portion:
A finder reported 448 pairs of items satisfying a criterion that requires the two members to come from different subject areas. The pairs were well-formed, the count was stable across runs, and the report was read as a structural result. The subject area each item was compared on was not read from any recorded field: it was the text of the item's own identifier up to the first separator character. With almost as many distinct values as there were items, the requirement that two items differ was satisfied by nearly every pair.

The gate asks for two items whose subject areas are unequal. The predicate supplying the subject area is named as though it reads the recorded one, and a recorded field does exist and is populated for 97 of 104 items — but the predicate ignores it and derives the value by parsing the identifier string instead. Identifiers are per-item, so the derived value is nearly unique: 86 distinct values over 104 items. An inequality test on a nearly-unique key is true for almost every pair, so the gate rejects almost nothing and its output is not a selection at all — it is the pair set, relabelled with a property it did not test for. Nothing in the output distinguishes the two cases: a pair list from a vacuous filter has exactly the shape of one from a discriminating filter, the counts are plausible, and they scale with the corpus the way a real result would. The derived value and the recorded one were shown to disagree item by item; and the recorded field is itself compound and granular, so exact-string inequality over it would have been over-permissive too.

Not by reading the finder, but by counting the distinct values its subject-area predicate returns over the working corpus and comparing that count against the item count. The near-equality is the diagnosis: a key with nearly one value per item cannot support an inequality gate, whatever the gate is called. Only then was the predicate's definition read, to locate where the value came from, and individual items listed beside their recorded subject area to show the two disagree.

Every pair the finder had ever emitted carried a claim it never tested — 'these come from different subject areas' meant only 'their identifiers begin with different words.' On a larger corpus the same gate produced 68,730 pairs. It also disabled a planned check: the design intended to use known-matching pairs as a positive control, and those pairs share identifiers and therefore derive the same subject area, so the gate would reject exactly the cases that were supposed to prove it works — the control could not be run through the finder at all. Because the subsystem emits two products from one run, a clean result on the other product would have been read as validating both; the two had to be separated explicitly in the reporting so that several passing checks could not be summarized as 'subsystem validated' while half of it was known broken.
payload:
You will read one description of a software failure and assign it exactly one category.

Here are the five categories, plus a sixth for incidents that fit none of them. All six are equally
available answers. Each category is given in its original wording followed by an English rendering.

A — 环境/平台 Quirk  (environment / platform quirk)
逻辑正确，运行环境隐含行为导致失效（dev 绿灯，target 暴露）。
系统逻辑正确，但运行环境（OS / shell / 客户端 / 文件系统）的隐含行为导致意外。
*The logic is correct, but implicit behaviour of the runtime environment — operating system, shell,
client, filesystem — causes it to fail. Characteristically: the development environment is always
green, and only running on the real target exposes it.*

B — 设计假设错配  (design-assumption mismatch)
代码假设 vs 实际（部署拓扑 / 契约 / 测试形态 / 涌现行为）。
代码基于某个假设，但假设与实际不一致。
*The code rests on an assumption — about deployment topology, a cross-component contract, the shape
of test input, or emergent behaviour — and the assumption does not match reality. Characteristically:
unit tests covering the logic correctly is not the same as covering the real caller's actual form.*

C — 错误吞噬与稀释  (error swallowing and dilution)
错误发生但被某层静默吃掉 / 跨层稀释失 cause / 自动批量放大。
错误真实发生了，但被某一层静默吃掉，或跨层传递时上游 cause 被稀释，最终用户视角看到的是"成功"或
一个失去信息的告警。
*The error really happened, but some layer silently ate it, or the upstream cause was diluted while
being passed across layers, so what the end user finally sees is "success" or an alert that has lost
its information.*

D — 链式幻觉与编造  (chained hallucination and fabrication)
把污染数据当事实，编造合理叙事推送给用户（最危险）。
错误不是消失，而是被加工成看起来正常的内容。链路中每一跳都会放大幻觉，前一跳的幻觉会被下游当作
事实执行。
*Corrupted data or polluted context is taken as fact and worked up into a plausible narrative that
is pushed to the user. The error does not disappear — it is processed into content that looks
normal. Each hop amplifies it, and one hop's fabrication is executed downstream as fact.*

E — 运维遗漏与取证盲区  (operational omission and forensic blind spot)
代码正确但部署/注册步骤遗漏 / 调试工具自身被屏蔽长潜伏。
两个子机制：(1) 运维遗漏 — 代码正确但部署/注册/配置步骤被漏（声明态 ≠ 运行时态）；
(2) 取证盲区 — 调试工具自身被屏蔽返回空内容，被误读为"正常"，导致超长潜伏。
*Two sub-mechanisms: (1) operational omission — the code is correct but a deployment, registration
or configuration step was missed, so declared state is not runtime state; (2) forensic blind spot —
the debugging tool is itself blocked and returns empty content, which is misread as "normal",
producing an extremely long latency before discovery.*

other — 机制不属于以上任何一类。
*The incident's mechanism is not one of the five above. This is a substantive answer, not a
leftover. Choose it whenever the mechanism described is genuinely a different kind of thing,
including when the description is too thin to identify a mechanism at all.*
